title: Number of Ways Where Square of Number Is Equal to Product of Two Numbers
summary: For arrays nums1 and nums2, count triplets of types where the square of an element from nums1 equals the product of two elements from nums2, and vice versa, with indices following the specified constraints.
statement: For arrays nums1 and nums2, count triplets of types where the square of an element from nums1 equals the product of two elements from nums2, and vice versa, with indices following the specified constraints.
constraints: Count triples where one squared value from either array equals the product of two values at distinct indices in the other array.
Occurrences at different indices count separately.
hints: Count value frequencies in the array supplying factor pairs.
For each squared value, iterate distinct factor values that divide it and look up the complementary factor.
Subtract one occurrence when both factors are equal, then divide ordered selections by two.
Run the calculation in both array directions and add the results.
editorial: Run the calculation in both array directions and add the results.

tests.explanation: Four squared equals two times eight, producing one valid triple.
Each squared one combines with every index pair in the opposite array, giving nine triples across both directions.
